Recommendation: separate Python 3.11 (or 3.12) venv for this model, kept apart from HNRad's 3.13 FastAPI backend, talking to it over a subprocess/CLI call.
verdicts.outputs: A 5-label multiclass mask over the input CT/CBCT: (1) maxilla/upper skull, (2) mandible, (3) upper teeth, (4) lower teeth, (5) mandibular (inferior alveolar) canal. Native output from nnUNetv2_predict is NIfTI (.nii.gz) label maps in the input geometry, so SimpleITK can read them directly and scikit-image/VTK marching cubes gives per-label surfaces for STL export. The 3D Slicer path wraps the same weights and produces a Slicer segmentation node with those five segments. Distribution: weights zip (Dataset112_DentalSegmentator_v100.zip, 229.7 MB) from Zenodo 10829675 for direct command-line nnU-Net use; GitHub release ships a similar zip under a different dataset id (Dataset111_453CT_v100). No landmarks, no osteotomy planes, no fibula geometry — HNRad still has to build canal centreline extraction, osteotomy plane placement and segment fitting on top of the masks.
verdicts.reason: Candidate is confirmed real and the summary is accurate, with two caveats that change how you should integrate it. CONFIRMED: repo exists at the stated URL, 189 stars, active (last push 2026-05-22), Apache-2.0 code, CC-BY-4.0 weights on Zenodo 10829675, five labels exactly as claimed including the mandibular canal. Validation is genuine and stronger than most: per PubMed, 470 CT/CBCT training scans, two hold-out test sets (internal n=133 pre-orthognathic, external n=123 from 5 institutions), mean DSC 92.2 +/- 6.3% internal and 94.2 +/- 7.4% external, NSD ~98%. Caveat: those are class-averaged figures; the abstract gives no per-structure number, and the canal is normally the weakest class in this task, so the canal mask must be treated as a draft the surgeon confirms, never as an automatic safety boundary. CPU is officially supported, not just tolerated: SegmentationWidget.py falls back to CPU with a dialog reading "Running the segmentation may take up to 1 hour", and it runs a single fold (folds="0"), not a 5-fold ensemble, which is the main reason CPU is tractable at all. For a 512x512x180 contrast neck CT expect meaningfully worse than that hour, because nnU-Net resamples to the dental plans' fine spacing and your FOV is far larger than a dental one; budget 1-3 h and watch RAM. Mitigation that probably matters more than any other tuning: crop to a mandible bounding box (threshold bone, take the largest inferior component) before handing the volume to nnU-Net — cuts voxels and runtime by a large factor. Second caveat, and the one real risk: open issue #41 (2026-07-30, no maintainer reply) is a Windows 11 CPU-only user on nnunetv2 2.8.1 getting "Detected old nnU-Net plans format. Attempting to reconstruct network architecture parameters." followed by "Background workers died... your RAM was full and the worker was killed by the OS." The 2024 weights are drifting out of compatibility with current nnU-Net, so pin an older nnunetv2 rather than taking latest. Third, unflagged by the candidate: domain shift. Weights were trained on dento-maxillo-facial CT/CBCT, not contrast-enhanced full-neck oncology CT. Validate on a handful of your own studies before trusting it, and expect the upper-skull/maxilla label to behave oddly where your FOV extends well beyond the training FOV. Nothing leaves the device: weights download once, inference is fully local. Install needs no admin — all pip wheels, no compilers, no CUDA-only ops.
verdicts.install_notes: Use a separate Python 3.11 venv (3.13 wheels exist for torch 2.8/cc3d/blosc2/imagecodecs, but older nnU-Net pins may not resolve there). pip install --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu torch; pip install nnunetv2==2.5.1 — pin it, since issue #41 shows 2.8.1 failing on Windows 11 CPU with "old nnU-Net plans format" then dead workers. Unzip Zenodo 10829675 into nnUNet_results; run nnUNetv2_predict -c 3d_fullres -f 0 -device cpu. Set pip --proxy.
